speaker: Doctor
text:
Welcome to the clinic. I understand you are experiencing dizziness, nausea, and imbalance; to help me narrow down the cause, can you tell me if these symptoms started suddenly or developed gradually?

Also, have you experienced any recent head trauma, fever, or hearing changes like ringing in your ears?

speaker: Patient
text: 27-year-old male. The patient reports a sustained sensation of the room spinning since this morning, which is low grade and constant. He occasionally feels nauseous and has taken diphenhydramine to help him sleep, which also alleviates his symptoms slightly. He mentions recent increased intake of garlic due to trying to recover from a cold a few days ago. Past medical history is unremarkable.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV) is unlikely due to the sustained nature of the vertigo; the clinical picture is more consistent with vestibular neuritis or labyrinthitis, possibly triggered by a recent upper respiratory infection despite the garlic mention. I will proceed with further assessment to confirm the diagnosis.
